Pre-Algebra Review

What You’ll Learn

Section titled “What You’ll Learn”

This review covers every major topic from Pre-Algebra in one place — variables, expressions, equations, inequalities, exponents, proportions, absolute value, and graphing. Each section has a quick refresher and a worked example so you can brush up before moving on.

Variables & Expressions

Section titled “Variables & Expressions”

A variable is a letter that stands for an unknown number. An expression combines variables, numbers, and operations (but no equals sign).

To evaluate an expression, substitute the given values and follow order of operations.

Evaluate 3x+2y−53x + 2y - 53x+2y−5 when x=4x = 4x=4 and y=3y = 3y=3:

3(4)+2(3)−5=12+6−5=13\begin{aligned} 3(4) + 2(3) - 5 &\\ = 12 + 6 - 5 &\\ = 13 \end{aligned}3(4)+2(3)−5=12+6−5=13​​

Signed Numbers

Section titled “Signed Numbers”

Same signs → add and keep the sign. Different signs → subtract and keep the sign of the larger absolute value.

For multiplication/division: same signs → positive, different signs → negative.

−8+5=−3(−6)×(−4)=2415÷(−3)=−5\begin{aligned} {-}8 + 5 &= {-}3 \\ ({-}6) \times ({-}4) &= 24 \\ 15 \div ({-}3) &= {-}5 \end{aligned}−8+5(−6)×(−4)15÷(−3)​=−3=24=−5​

Order of Operations

Section titled “Order of Operations”

PEMDAS: Parentheses → Exponents → Multiply/Divide (left to right) → Add/Subtract (left to right).

Evaluate 4+3(2x−1)24 + 3(2x - 1)^24+3(2x−1)2 when x=2x = 2x=2:

4+3(2(2)−1)2=4+3(4−1)2=4+3(3)2=4+3(9)=4+27=31\begin{aligned} 4 + 3(2(2) - 1)^2 &\\ = 4 + 3(4 - 1)^2 &\\ = 4 + 3(3)^2 &\\ = 4 + 3(9) &\\ = 4 + 27 = 31 \end{aligned}4+3(2(2)−1)2=4+3(4−1)2=4+3(3)2=4+3(9)=4+27=31​​

Combining Like Terms & Distributive Property

Section titled “Combining Like Terms & Distributive Property”

Like terms have the same variable and exponent. Combine by adding/subtracting coefficients.

The distributive property: a(b+c)=ab+aca(b + c) = ab + aca(b+c)=ab+ac.

Simplify 2(3x+4)−5x+12(3x + 4) - 5x + 12(3x+4)−5x+1:

2(3x+4)−5x+1=6x+8−5x+1=x+9\begin{aligned} 2(3x + 4) - 5x + 1 &\\ = 6x + 8 - 5x + 1 &\\ = x + 9 \end{aligned}2(3x+4)−5x+1=6x+8−5x+1=x+9​​

Solving Equations

Section titled “Solving Equations”

One-step: Do the inverse operation on both sides.

x+12=20x=8\begin{aligned} x + 12 &= 20 \\ x &= 8 \end{aligned}x+12x​=20=8​

Two-step: Undo add/subtract first, then multiply/divide.

3x−7=143x=21x=7\begin{aligned} 3x - 7 &= 14 \\ 3x &= 21 \\ x &= 7 \end{aligned}3x−73xx​=14=21=7​

Variables on both sides: Move all variable terms to one side first.

5x+3=2x+183x+3=183x=15x=5\begin{aligned} 5x + 3 &= 2x + 18 \\ 3x + 3 &= 18 \\ 3x &= 15 \\ x &= 5 \end{aligned}5x+33x+33xx​=2x+18=18=15=5​

Check: 5(5)+3=285(5) + 3 = 285(5)+3=28 and 2(5)+18=282(5) + 18 = 282(5)+18=28 ✓

Inequalities

Section titled “Inequalities”

Solve like equations, but flip the sign when multiplying/dividing by a negative.

−2x+6>12−2x>6x<−3(flip: divided by −2)\begin{aligned} {-}2x + 6 &> 12 \\ {-}2x &> 6 \\ x &< {-}3 \quad \text{(flip: divided by }{-}2\text{)} \end{aligned}−2x+6−2xx​>12>6<−3(flip: divided by −2)​

Graph: open circle at −3-3−3, shade left.

Exponents & Powers

Section titled “Exponents & Powers”

ana^nan means multiply aaa by itself nnn times. Key rules:

  • a0=1a^0 = 1a0=1
  • a−n=1ana^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}a−n=an1​
  • am×an=am+na^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}am×an=am+n
25=324−2=11632×33=35=243\begin{aligned} 2^5 &= 32 \\ 4^{-2} &= \frac{1}{16} \\ 3^2 \times 3^3 &= 3^5 = 243 \end{aligned}254−232×33​=32=161​=35=243​

Proportions & Ratios

Section titled “Proportions & Ratios”

A proportion is two equal ratios: ab=cd\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d}ba​=dc​. Cross-multiply to solve.

A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for 18 muffins. How much for 30 muffins?

318=x303×30=18x90=18xx=5 cups\begin{aligned} \frac{3}{18} &= \frac{x}{30} \\ 3 \times 30 &= 18x \\ 90 &= 18x \\ x &= 5 \text{ cups} \end{aligned}183​3×3090x​=30x​=18x=18x=5 cups​

Absolute Value

Section titled “Absolute Value”

∣x∣|x|∣x∣ is the distance from 0 — always positive or zero. Equations split into two cases.

Solve ∣2x−1∣=7|2x - 1| = 7∣2x−1∣=7:

Case 1:

2x−1=72x=8x=4\begin{aligned} 2x - 1 &= 7 \\ 2x &= 8 \\ x &= 4 \end{aligned}2x−12xx​=7=8=4​

Case 2:

2x−1=−72x=−6x=−3\begin{aligned} 2x - 1 &= {-}7 \\ 2x &= {-}6 \\ x &= {-}3 \end{aligned}2x−12xx​=−7=−6=−3​

Check: ∣2(4)−1∣=∣7∣=7|2(4) - 1| = |7| = 7∣2(4)−1∣=∣7∣=7 ✓ and ∣2(−3)−1∣=∣−7∣=7|2(-3) - 1| = |-7| = 7∣2(−3)−1∣=∣−7∣=7 ✓

Word Problems

Section titled “Word Problems”

Translate words into equations, solve, and check.

You earn 18 dollars per hour and need at least 500 dollars for rent. How many hours minimum?

18h≥500h≥27.8\begin{aligned} 18h &\geq 500 \\ h &\geq 27.8 \end{aligned}18hh​≥500≥27.8​

You need at least 28 hours.

Basic Graphing

Section titled “Basic Graphing”

Points are (x,y)(x, y)(x,y). Lines in slope-intercept form: y=mx+by = mx + by=mx+b.

Graph y=2x−1y = 2x - 1y=2x−1:

xxxyyy
000−1-1−1
111111
222333
−1-1−1−3-3−3

Slope m=2m = 2m=2 (up 2, right 1). Y-intercept b=−1b = -1b=−1 (crosses y-axis at (0,−1)(0, -1)(0,−1)).

Mixed Practice

Section titled “Mixed Practice”

Try these on your own before checking the quiz:

  1. Evaluate 4(x−3)+2x4(x - 3) + 2x4(x−3)+2x when x=5x = 5x=5 → 4(2)+10=184(2) + 10 = 184(2)+10=18
  2. Solve 6x+1=3x+166x + 1 = 3x + 166x+1=3x+16 → x=5x = 5x=5
  3. Solve −3y≤21-3y \leq 21−3y≤21 → y≥−7y \geq -7y≥−7
  4. Simplify 53×5−15^3 \times 5^{-1}53×5−1 → 52=255^2 = 2552=25
  5. Solve 47=x21\frac{4}{7} = \frac{x}{21}74​=21x​ → x=12x = 12x=12
  6. Solve ∣x−4∣=9|x - 4| = 9∣x−4∣=9 → x=13x = 13x=13 or x=−5x = -5x=−5

You’ve Got This

You’ve covered a lot in Pre-Algebra — from letters standing for numbers to solving equations, inequalities, and even graphing. Each skill builds on the last. Pick one problem type at a time, check your work, and celebrate what you’ve already mastered. You’re ready for Algebra Basics whenever you are.
